content.title: 60th Ave Improvements
content.summary: Improvements to W. 60th Avenue from Tennyson to Sheridan are set to begin on April 27, 2026, with construction expected to last 4 to 6 months. The project includes road widening, repaving, and the addition of safer bike lanes and wider sidewalks, while maintaining two-way traffic when possible and implementing alternating one-way traffic with flaggers. The first segment from Tennyson to Wolff was completed in 2025, featuring a two-way separated bike lane and updated sidewalks.
content.body:
## Updates

Update 4/23/26

Construction activities from Wolff to Sheridan are schedule to**begin as soon as Monday, April 27.**

- **Two-way traffic** will be maintained when possible
- **One-way, alternating traffic**with flaggers may be necessary
- **Sidewalk closure**on the north side of W. 60th Ave.
- **On-street parking** will be limited

## Overview

W. 60th Avenue from Tennyson to Sheridan is being improved in two segments to include safer bike lanes and wider sidewalks in some areas. The road will also be repaved and curb ramps updated to ADA standards as a part of this project.

- Segment 1: Tennyson to Wolff (complete)
- Segment 2: Wolff to Sheridan (early 2026)

The City also has a grant for a [separate bike and pedestrian project along Tennyson Street](/1031) that is currently in the design phase.

## Segment 2: Wolff to Sheridan

Work is expected to begin in early 2026, **as soon as the end of April**. Once work begins, construction is expected to take 4 to 6 months to complete. Work is weather permitting.

### Improvements

- Road widening, repaving, and new striping
- Sidewalk replacement and widening to 6 ft. on the north side
- Push-to-cross signal at Wolff Street for cyclists and pedestrians

![Aerial view of improvements between Wolff to Sheridan with shared bike lanes](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6867)

### Construction impacts

- Working hours 7 am to 7 pm
- Additional construction noise and traffic
- Lane closures with flaggers directing alternating one-way traffic
  - Two-way traffic will be maintained when possible
- Sidewalk closures on the north and south side (one at a time)
- Driveway access will be maintained
  - Any driveway access limitations will be coordinated with individual property owners
- On-street parking will be limited
- Road repaving and restriping new lane markings
- Construction staging area at former Early College of Arvada

![Street view of the improvements along 60th Avenue at the Wolff intersection facing west](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6865)

![aerial view of improvements to 60th and Wolff intersection with bike lane and crosswalk](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6872)

## Segment 1: Tennyson to Wolff

Segment 1 from Tennyson to Wolff was completed in 2025.

### Improvements

- ### Two-way separated bike lane with delineators on the south side of the road
- South side parking removed to make room for bike lanes
- Road repaving and restriping

![Aerial view of improvements between Tennyson and Wolff with south side two way separated bike lanes](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6866)

![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=927)

On the south side of the street, the previous parking has been turned into a two lane bike path that is separated by delineators from the two-way vehicle traffic. Parking is retained on the north side of the street. Pedestrian sidewalks exist on both the north and south sides of the street.

## Contact

Please submit a ticket through [Ask Arvada](/898) and a team member will be in touch.

## About the Project

The two-way separated bike lane will create a safer connection from Tennyson to the RTD Gold Strike G-Line Station. This bike lane removed parking on the south side of the road from Wolff St. to Tennyson. W. 60th Ave. from Wolff to Sheridan is being widened with a new 6 ft. sidewalk on the north side. The wider road will help accommodate parking on both sides of the road and a shared bike lane.

The bike lane will connect to new bike lanes on Tennyson St to create a safe, connected bikeway between the Clear Creek Trail and the Gold Strike Station. Learn more about the Tennyson portion of the project on the [Tennyson Street project page](/1031).
